title: After the Deal: Consolidating Platforms After Acquisitions
basis: Reconstructed on 2026-11-12 from the published index.md (paragraph for paragraph, in its own order) and spec.md (accepted 2026-10-21), which it replaces. Intent outcome, acceptance criteria AC-1 to AC-3, thesis and role are copied unchanged from the platform-consolidation entry in journal-spec.json; the hand-off uses organizing-marketplace-engineering's transition_in. Units added by this conversion: roadmap p04, one lead-in each for Trade-offs (p39) and Vertical Differences (p41), and a synthesis paragraph p52 before the published hand-off.

know: The integration options for an acquired business (hold separate, federate under group controls, share services beneath it, replatform onto a sibling, merge brands, divest) and the regulatory, contractual and ownership conditions that rule each out.

The consolidation sequence: day-one controls; invisible and contractual capabilities, with payments as a contract; trust and identity; shared engines; the product platform last and optional, each with a measured gate.
The synergy case as a ledger with dis-synergies, double running and separation cost, and brand migration as a separate workstream (site moves, accounts, partner endpoints, business-user notice).
believe: An acquisition should be consolidated from the invisible to the visible, because the product carries the liquidity the deal paid for.
A synergy case is a hypothesis to be tracked against dated evidence, and a revenue line that depends on data needs a named permission.
can_do: Write an integration decision record for an acquired marketplace.
Challenge a deal model's technology and data-dependent revenue lines before the price is agreed.
Plan a rebrand that does not compound with a platform migration.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Given an integration plan that moves the product first, the reader names what is out of order and the sequence and gates that replace it.
acceptance_criteria.probe: A group buys a national property portal. The integration plan rebrands it onto the group brand in month four, moves listings and search onto a sibling marketplace's platform in month ten, and leaves login, the moderation tool and agency billing for year three. The synergy case lists only savings, including revenue from using the acquired CRM's customer data to sell the group's packages. Using only this chapter: what is wrong, and what do you propose?
acceptance_criteria.expected: The sequence is inverted: trust and identity should consolidate before the product, which goes last with its own investment case; migrate to the group target, not to a sibling scheduled for replacement; gate each stage on the acquired marketplace's liquidity metrics, not dates; keep the rebrand apart from the platform move and start a second traffic-affecting change only when organic sessions are back near baseline; run the synergy case as a ledger with traffic loss, double running and separation cost; and require a named permission for the data-based revenue line, which a neutrality commitment may forbid.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A reader of the opening alone (the callouts and the paragraphs before the first heading) can predict the chapter's sections.
acceptance_criteria.probe: After reading only the callouts and the paragraphs before the first heading: what will this chapter discuss, in what order, and with what kind of evidence?
acceptance_criteria.expected: Choosing an integration option, sequencing consolidation from controls to product with gates, running the synergy case as a ledger, and brand migration; the terms consolidation sequence, synergy case and brand migration; evidence from the public record of classifieds acquisitions (eBay, AVIV, OLX, Adevinta) and the fictional Veldmark's Casavista and Keybridge integrations.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A reverse outline of the chapter, written without the spec, lists the same controlling ideas in the same order as the post spec's sections and paragraphs.

audience.who: Chief and enterprise architects, CTOs and integration leads of marketplace groups that buy and sometimes sell marketplaces, and the finance and corporate-development partners who write synergy cases with them.
already_knows: APIs, databases, event streams, search engines and Kubernetes; what an acquisition and a deal model are in general.

From earlier chapters: Veldmark (fictional) and its brands Tradeyard, Motorvane, Hearthly and Keybridge, Common Ground, Veldmark ID, Ingrid Halvorsen, Henrik de Boer, Lucía Ortega and the architecture advice forum; liquidity and its metrics (liquidity-and-network-effects); the Barcelona fake-rental ring (fraud-prevention, identity-and-verification); the Keybridge neutrality commitment of March 2027; the marketplace profile register (marketplace-taxonomy); the redirect registry (web-and-seo-architecture); the failure patterns Deal-Shaped Architecture, The Forced Fit and Ghost Inventory.

From Part VII: the tenancy model and tenant-separable shared capabilities of multi-country-platforms; from the Part VIII introduction, that the part asks in what order the earlier decisions are carried out.
does_not_know: The terms this chapter owns: consolidation sequence, synergy case, brand migration; and the integration options by name.
Deal vocabulary: run-rate synergies, dis-synergies, separation cost, carve-out and transitional services, merger-control remedies.
Brand-migration mechanics: site-move redirects and the Change of Address tool, app store identity and design tokens, sender-domain ramp-up, the P2B notice period.
The Casavista integration figures, the consolidation review of 9 November 2027 and the synergy ledger.

thesis.question: When a group acquires marketplaces, what should it consolidate, when, and how?
thesis.claim: A group should choose an integration option for each acquired marketplace in a decision record within the first month after signing, letting merger remedies, commitments to customers and the expected holding period rule options out before technical fit; consolidate from the invisible to the visible (day-one controls, then infrastructure, data, advertising and payment contracts, then trust and identity, then shared engines), leaving the core listing and search product last and only with its own investment case; gate each stage on the acquired marketplace's liquidity metrics rather than on dates; run the synergy case as a ledger that counts traffic loss, double running and separation cost and names the permission behind every revenue line that uses data; and keep any brand migration a separate workstream that does not overlap a platform migration.
thesis.disputed_by: The common deal-team plan: replatform the acquired marketplace onto the acquirer's or a sibling's product stack and rebrand it on the deal's timetable, moving search, listings and the brand first because that makes the acquisition visible, and tracking synergies as a spreadsheet of savings; or the opposite habit of leaving every acquired stack untouched indefinitely.
thesis.so_what: A Chief Architect who accepts this reviews every technology synergy and every data-dependent revenue synergy before the price is agreed, owns the consolidation sequence while the deal team owns the targets, reviews the synergy ledger quarterly with finance, pauses any stage whose liquidity gate fails, migrates to the group target rather than to a sibling due for replacement, and designs every integration so that it can be undone if the business is later sold.
thesis.how_why: Veldmark replatformed Casavista product-first: the rebrand on 9 March 2026 cost 19% of organic sessions in six weeks, and listings and search moved in September 2026 before traffic had recovered, so the cause of each dip could not be separated. Login, the moderation review tool and agency billing stayed on Casavista's code at about €2.6 million a year, and in July 2027 the Barcelona ring's 26 accounts had proved no more than an e-mail address. By October 2027 the deal had delivered €9.6 million of €18 million in synergies, at €11 million of one-off cost against €6 million planned. Keybridge's €7 million cross-selling line was forbidden by the March 2027 neutrality commitment. The recommended order reverses Casavista's because the invisible layers move without users noticing, trust and identity gain value as signals are pooled and are where fraud concentrates when left behind, and the product carries the liquidity the deal paid for, so it moves last and only after the gates show the lower stages held.

supporting_claims.claim: An acquirer chooses an integration option for each acquired business (hold separate, federate under group controls, share services beneath, replatform onto a sibling, merge brands, divest) in a recorded decision, and merger remedies, commitments to customers and the expected holding period rule options out before technical fit is considered.

Capabilities move onto group platforms from the invisible to the visible and from pooled value to mere cost: day-one controls, then infrastructure, data, advertising and payment contracts, then trust and identity, then shared engines, with the core listing and search product last, optional and on its own investment case, and always to the group target rather than to a sibling due for replacement.
Each stage is gated on the acquired marketplace's own liquidity metrics, not on the plan's dates, and a second traffic-affecting change waits until organic sessions have recovered.

A synergy case is a hypothesis run as a ledger that counts dis-synergies, double running and separation cost beside the savings, tracks each line against dated evidence, and names the permission behind every revenue line that uses data.

A brand migration is an architectural workstream (domains and redirects, accounts, apps, e-mail, partner endpoints, legal notice) that is kept apart from any platform migration so that one traffic risk lands at a time.

role.contribution: Sets the order and the gates in which an acquired marketplace's capabilities move onto group platforms, and the synergy ledger that keeps the deal honest.

trade-offs, verticals, failure-modes, ca-view, questions: the book's standard judging sections

flow.rationale: The scene states the problem (synergies behind, costs over, a forbidden line, a fraud gap) before any solution. The concepts give the terms the answer needs, including the synergy case the ledger later tracks; the architecture gives the general answer, with gates as measured conditions; the review applies it to the scene's problem, which only works once the options, the sequence, its gates and the synergy case have been defined. Placed before the architecture, the review's 'inverted sequence' would have nothing to be inverted against. The judging sections weigh the whole design and come last.

hook.content: A marketplace acquisition is usually justified in two sentences: the target is a market leader, and owning it alongside the group's other marketplaces will save money and grow revenue.

bridge.from_reader_world: The deal rationale every reader has seen: a market leader bought for savings and growth.
bridge.to_topic: The first sentence is about liquidity the acquirer must not damage, the second about platforms it must change, and the record of classifieds groups shows how often that goes wrong.

thesis_statement.text: Choose an integration option per business, with regulation, commitments and a likely sale ruling options out; consolidate from the bottom up, invisible and pooled first and the product last, gated on liquidity metrics; run the synergy case as a ledger with dis-synergies and separation cost; decouple brand migrations from platform migrations.

roadmap.placement: Paragraph p04, with the IN THIS CHAPTER callout.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: A marketplace acquisition is justified by two sentences, one about liquidity the acquirer must not damage and one about platforms it must change, so consolidation is the work of changing the platform without damaging the liquidity while both compete for the same months, teams and risk budget.

advances_thesis.how: States the tension the sequence and its gates resolve.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Because classifieds groups were assembled almost entirely by acquisition, their public record on consolidation is rich, and it shows more reversals than finished integrations.

evidence.what: eBay bought national leaders and kept their brands; Axel Springer combined property portals into AVIV; Naspers rebranded acquired sites as OLX; Adevinta bought eBay Classifieds Group, integrated part of it and, under new owners, decentralized and sold businesses.
evidence.shows: Shows four groups taking different paths and the last one reversing, which is the record's main lesson.

advances_thesis.how: Grounds the options and the cost of reversal in the public record.

sections.heading: Setting the Scene at Veldmark: Where Are the Casavista Synergies?
sections.controlling_idea: By October 2027 Veldmark's two real-estate acquisitions had delivered about half their promised synergies at nearly twice the planned cost, one synergy line had become forbidden, and the unconsolidated Spanish login had let a fraud ring in.

advances_thesis.how: Gives the case whose inverted sequence and spreadsheet of savings the chapter's claims correct.

flow.rationale: The owner's question comes first, then the evidence behind it in the order the reader needs it (Casavista's numbers, Keybridge's forbidden line, the July fraud), then the review that answers it; the review's three arguments make sense only once all three problems are on the table.

transition_in.carries_over: The tension between liquidity and platforms and the chapter's terms.
transition_in.introduces: Veldmark's synergy question as the running case.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: On 14 October 2027 Henrik de Boer forwarded Ingrid Halvorsen the private-equity owner's question of where the synergies paid for in Veldmark's two real-estate acquisitions were.

evidence.what: Thu 14 Oct 2027; the owner's operating partner, ahead of the 2028 budget; two businesses bought into the real-estate portfolio in two years.
evidence.shows: Sets the question the chapter answers.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Casavista, bought in 2025 and rebranded Hearthly.es in 2026, had delivered €9.6 million of €18 million in promised run-rate synergies at €11 million of one-off cost against €6 million planned, while its login, review tool and agency billing still ran on Casavista's code at about €2.6 million a year.

evidence.what: Deal case €18M by end 2027 (€8M platform and hosting, €4M overheads, €6M revenue); Oct 2027 tracker €9.6M (tech €3.9M, overheads €3.6M, revenue €2.1M); one-off cost €11M vs €6M; listings and search on Hearthly's Google Cloud platform since 2026; login, review tool and agency billing on Casavista code and hosting at ~€2.6M a year.
evidence.shows: Shows the synergies lagging and the costs overrunning, with the trust-critical parts left behind.

transition_in.carries_over: The two businesses behind the owner's question.
transition_in.introduces: The first business, Casavista, and its numbers.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Keybridge's €7 million cross-selling line, which depended on using its 9,800 agency customers' data to sell them Hearthly packages, had been forbidden by the March 2027 neutrality commitment.

evidence.what: Keybridge bought 2024; €7M/yr revenue synergy from agency insight; March 2027 commitment that no Keybridge agency data be used by Hearthly for ranking or sales targeting.
evidence.shows: Shows a synergy line that is not delayed but forbidden.

transition_in.introduces: The second business, Keybridge, and its line.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: In July 2027 the Barcelona fake-rental ring exploited the still-unconsolidated Spanish login, showing that the parts of the acquisition left unconsolidated were the ones that mattered most for trust.

evidence.shows: Shows the cost of leaving trust and identity for last.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Ingrid's consolidation review of 9 November 2027, the thread of the chapter, argued that the synergy case had been sequenced in the wrong order, had counted only savings and contained one line that should never have been written.

evidence.what: Consolidation review presented to the board Tue 9 Nov 2027.
evidence.shows: Names the answer the chapter follows.

transition_in.introduces: The review's three arguments that answer them.

sections.heading: Concepts: Options, Sequences, Synergies and Brands
sections.controlling_idea: Four concepts frame consolidation: the integration option chosen per business, the consolidation sequence ordered from invisible to visible, the synergy case with its usually missing parts, and the brand migration as an architectural event.

advances_thesis.how: Defines the terms each later section argues with, with dated public cases for each.

flow.rationale: The option comes first because it decides whether any sequence is needed; the sequence before the synergy case because synergies depend on stages; the brand migration last because it is the one move the sequence keeps separate. Each definition is followed by the public case that shows it, so no example arrives before its term.

transition_in.introduces: The concepts those arguments use.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: An acquirer has five integration options plus the option to sell, and they differ in what is shared and in how reversible the result is.

evidence.what: Hold separate, federate under group controls, share services beneath, replatform onto a sibling, merge brands, divest; each with what changes, what stays, reversibility and a documented example (eBay/Marktplaats 2004, Adevinta 2019–2023, iBazar to Vivanuncios 2015, OLX rebrands 2014, CMA remedies 2021).
evidence.shows: Shows that each option is real and dated, and that reversibility falls as sharing rises.

advances_thesis.how: Defines the options the decision record chooses among.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Options are chosen per business and may be combined over time, but an acquisition without a recorded option drifts into Deal-Shaped Architecture by inertia.

advances_thesis.how: Argues for a recorded choice.

transition_in.introduces: How they are chosen and what happens when none is.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Commercial integration can run years ahead of technical integration, as two documented property-portal cases show.

evidence.what: Immowelt and Immonet combined in 2015, renamed AVIV Germany in 2024 and still running both brands; AVIV's Ultimmo (2022), one professional offer across SeLoger, Logic-Immo and Meilleurs Agents.
evidence.shows: Shows hold separate lasting at the brand level while the companies combine; the paragraph's last sentence says so.

advances_thesis.how: Shows that holding separate is a legitimate long-term option.

transition_in.introduces: Commercial integration ahead of technical integration.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: A consolidation sequence is the ordered set of gated stages through which an acquired marketplace's capabilities move onto group platforms, answering which capability moves next, what must be true first and what would stop it.

advances_thesis.how: Defines the sequence and its gates.

transition_in.introduces: The second term, the consolidation sequence.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Two rules set the order, moving what users cannot see before what they can and what gains value from pooling before what only saves cost, and the core listing and search experience fails both, so it comes last and often never.

evidence.what: Figure 1: a building renovated from the foundation up beneath an unchanged storefront.
evidence.shows: Shows the bottom-up order with the visible product untouched.

advances_thesis.how: Gives the reasoning behind the order.

transition_in.introduces: The two rules that order it.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: A synergy case is the quantified hypothesis that combining a business with the group raises profit, and of its four parts (cost, revenue, dis-synergies, separation cost) deal models usually show only two.

evidence.what: Four parts with typical lines and whether they usually appear in the deal model.
evidence.shows: Shows which parts deal models leave out.

evidence.what: Figure 2: a scale weighing savings against traffic loss, churn, double running and separation cost.
evidence.shows: Shows the case as a ledger with both sides.

advances_thesis.how: Defines the case and its missing parts.

transition_in.carries_over: The order in which capabilities move.
transition_in.introduces: The third term, the synergy case that funds the moves.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Adevinta's eCG deal shows the parts a deal model leaves out arriving later: integration expenses and a forced rebrand during integration, and separation cost after the take-private.

evidence.what: €130–165M run-rate cost-synergy target (Adevinta, 2021); €69M eCG integration expenses in 2023 plus €15M for the eBay Kleinanzeigen rebrand (Annual Report 2023); 'parallel running of central and local services during a transitional period' (Strategic Report 2025).
evidence.shows: Shows dis-synergies and separation cost appearing after the synergies they were never netted against.

advances_thesis.how: Grounds the ledger in a public case.

transition_in.carries_over: The four parts of a synergy case.
transition_in.introduces: A public deal in which the missing parts arrived.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: A brand migration moves users, sellers, partners and search-engine presence from one consumer brand to another, and it is an architectural event because the brand is embedded in domains, URLs, app identities, sender reputations, partner endpoints, legal entities and contracts.

advances_thesis.how: Defines the brand migration as architecture.

transition_in.carries_over: The synergy case, which a rebrand can cost.
transition_in.introduces: The fourth term, the brand migration.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The best-documented brand migration, Kleinanzeigen's, was forced by contract and was carried out two years apart from its platform migration.

evidence.what: eBay brand not usable beyond 2024; rebrand cost €15M in 2023; Kleinanzeigen from 16 May 2023 with the old domain kept accessible for several more years; a 2025 engineering post on migrating the whole platform with parallel running and per-user switching behind a reverse proxy.
evidence.shows: Shows a rebrand and a platform migration done as separate programs.

advances_thesis.how: Shows brand and platform migrations decoupled in practice.

transition_in.introduces: The industry's best-documented case.

sections.heading: Architecture: The Consolidation Sequence
sections.controlling_idea: The architecture of consolidation is a choice of option by four questions, a staged sequence whose gates are measured conditions resting on estate hygiene, and a brand migration run as its own workstream.

advances_thesis.how: Turns the concepts into the decision, the stages, the gates and the workstreams.

flow.rationale: The steps follow what each needs first: the option decides whether any sequence runs; hygiene is the precondition every stage needs, so it comes before the stages it gates; the stages and their placements follow; the brand migration comes last because the sequence keeps it apart. Putting the brand workstream before the stages would invite the reader to treat it as one of them, and putting hygiene after the stages (as first published) made a precondition arrive after what it conditions.

transition_in.introduces: The architecture that applies them, starting with the first decision after signing.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The integration option is the first architectural decision after signing, made with four questions.

evidence.what: Figure 3: choosing an integration option; regulation, commitments and expected holding period remove options before technology is considered.
evidence.shows: Shows the decision as a sequence of questions.

advances_thesis.how: Gives the decision procedure.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The questions are ordered by how absolute they are: a remedy or a commitment to customers rules integration out whatever its savings, a likely sale rules out deep sharing, and only then do the two questions of fit arise (same vertical and market as a group brand; an investment case for product convergence).

evidence.what: Keybridge's neutrality commitment as a commitment that rules out integration.
evidence.shows: Ties the rule to the running case.

advances_thesis.how: Explains why constraints come before technical fit.

transition_in.introduces: Why they come in that order.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The later stages depend on a prerequisite acquisitions rarely satisfy, an estate described well enough to move, and OLX's 2026 account of OLX Motors is a public checklist of that hygiene.

evidence.what: User identification standardized across 71 services, 'with 73% now using modern UUIDs'; 45 components moved to a central secrets manager; backup compliance for tier-1 and tier-2 databases; one deployment-notification service across more than 60 services.
evidence.shows: Shows hygiene work that is not consolidation but precedes it.

advances_thesis.how: Shows what the sequence depends on.

transition_in.introduces: The hygiene every stage of the sequence needs first.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Before trust and identity move, the author requires one identifier per user and seller, an inventory of every copy of listing and user data, events mapped to the group's listing event contract and a list of partner integrations with owners.

advances_thesis.how: Sets a concrete gate.

transition_in.introduces: The minimum the author would require.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The reference sequence moves capabilities in stages from day-one controls to an optional product platform, each more visible than the last, and its gates, each a measured condition that includes the acquired marketplace's liquidity against its baseline rather than a date, matter more than its stage boundaries.

evidence.what: Figure 4: the consolidation sequence; each gate is a measured condition, not a date.
evidence.shows: Shows the stages and gates.

evidence.what: Stages 0–4 with capabilities, why at this point, and the gate to the next stage (risk register, visibility in group tooling, detection and login success at baseline, relevance and billing parity, own investment case).
evidence.shows: Shows each gate as a measured condition.

advances_thesis.how: Gives the order and the gates.

transition_in.introduces: The stages and gates that can start once it is in place.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Payments sit in stage 1 as a contract, not as code, because consolidating payment-provider relationships is invisible to users and often worth more than merging checkout code.

evidence.what: Worldline's 2022 release named Marktplaats and eBay Kleinanzeigen as clients of Online Payment Platform.
evidence.shows: Shows two marketplaces sharing a provider while keeping their own flows.

advances_thesis.how: Explains one placement in the sequence.

transition_in.introduces: Why payments are in stage 1.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Identity sits in stage 2, not stage 1, because a login change is visible to every user and must be planned with the trust capabilities that depend on it.

advances_thesis.how: Explains a second placement.

transition_in.carries_over: Why payments sit where they do.
transition_in.introduces: Why identity sits where it does.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The governing rule for brand migrations is to decouple them from platform migrations, because together they produce a ranking drop nobody can attribute, roll back or fix quickly.

advances_thesis.how: States the decoupling rule.

transition_in.carries_over: The capability stages and their placements.
transition_in.introduces: The brand migration, which the sequence keeps separate.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: A brand migration touches more systems than its sponsors expect.

evidence.what: Figure 5: the workstreams of a brand migration and their dependencies; most are invisible in the brand plan and visible on switch day.
evidence.shows: Shows the breadth of systems a rebrand touches.

advances_thesis.how: Shows the scope of the workstream.

transition_in.introduces: How much a brand migration touches.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Each workstream of a brand migration (domains and URLs, accounts, apps, e-mail and notifications, partners, legal) has its own rules.

evidence.what: Google Search Central site-move guidance (updated 2026): permanent redirects, short chains, redirects kept generally at least one year, Change of Address tool, temporary ranking fluctuation.
evidence.shows: Gives the rules for domains and URLs.

evidence.what: Kleinanzeigen accounts carried over without re-registration (press reporting, not verified against a primary source).
evidence.shows: Shows the accounts rule in a real case.

evidence.what: mobile.de: 'the rebranding itself was the final step and took only two weeks to implement once the base refactoring was done'.
evidence.shows: Shows design tokens making a brand a configuration value.

evidence.what: Regulation (EU) 2019/1150, Article 3: changes to business users' terms notified at least 15 days ahead.
evidence.shows: Gives the legal notice rule.

advances_thesis.how: Gives the workstream rules.

sections.heading: In Practice: Veldmark's Consolidation Review
sections.controlling_idea: Veldmark's review found Casavista's sequence inverted, resequenced the remaining work to the group target, replaced the synergy spreadsheets with a ledger, held Keybridge separate on purpose and settled the Polish overlap as a portfolio decision.

advances_thesis.how: Applies the option, sequence, gate and ledger to the running case with numbers.

flow.rationale: The reconstruction of what went wrong comes first, because the revised sequence and the ledger are answers to it; the ledger follows the resequencing because its dates come from the new plan; Keybridge and the Polish overlap close the section as the cases where the right answer was not to consolidate.

transition_in.introduces: Veldmark's review, which applies them.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Ingrid's review tested Casavista against the sequence by reconstructing the integration from the 2025 deal case and the 2026–2027 program records.

evidence.what: 2025 deal case and 'replatform onto Hearthly France, then rebrand'; Mon 9 Mar 2026 rebrand, organic sessions −19% in six weeks and −5% by Sep 2026; Sep 2026 listings and search moved, second dip; late 2026 login, review tool and billing deferred, €8M line stalled at €3.9M; July 2027 Barcelona ring.

advances_thesis.how: Lays out the inverted sequence as evidence.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The sequence was inverted: the product moved first because a replatform plan starts there and it makes the deal visible, while trust and identity, whose value grows with pooling, were left for last.

evidence.what: Figure 6: a new storefront on a cracked foundation versus a solid trust-and-identity foundation beneath an unchanged storefront.
evidence.shows: Shows the inverted and the recommended order.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The rebrand and the platform move were six months apart but the second began before the first had recovered, so the review set a rule that a second traffic-affecting change waits until organic sessions are within 3% of baseline or the board accepts the risk in writing.

advances_thesis.how: Sets the recovery gate.

transition_in.introduces: A second fault, the timing of the two traffic events.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The review resequenced the remaining work on the principle of migrating to the target, not to the sibling, using Common Ground's dates.

evidence.what: Moderation review tool to the shared T&S platform Q1 2028; private-landlord verification (L4) live in Q4 2027, ahead of the T&S move; login federated with Veldmark ID 2028, migrated 2029; agency billing to the group catalog in the second half of 2028 after a shadow billing cycle; Casavista hosting switched off end of 2029.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Consolidations fail when the synergy case precedes the architecture, the product moves first, migrations overlap, work moves to a sibling, revenue lines rest on forbidden data, scope is assumed at signing, the acquired organization is forgotten or no exit path exists.

conclusion.heading: From Sequence to Organization
conclusion.synthesis: The option, the order, the gates, the ledger and the separate brand workstream are one mechanism: the order decides which synergies arrive, the liquidity gates decide when, and the ledger prices every delay, so a group that runs them together protects the liquidity it bought while changing the platform beneath it, which Casavista's product-first plan did not.
conclusion.so_what: With the sequence and the ledger in hand, a Chief Architect can tell the owner where the synergies are, and which ones depend on which stage, before the owner has to ask.

callback.to: The opening's two sentences that justify an acquisition (liquidity not to damage, platforms to change) and Henrik de Boer's question of where the synergies were.
callback.how: The conclusion shows that the two sentences compete hardest when the platform moves product first, and that the review's answer to the question was a sequence and a ledger.

takeaway.content: Record the option, sequence the capabilities bottom-up behind liquidity gates, run the synergy case as a ledger and keep the brand migration apart.

hand_off.carries_over: Platform-consolidation's closing: a consolidation sequence says what moves and when, but not who owns each capability once it has moved or how the acquired engineers become part of the group.
